collection_type: Annotated source links and reuse notes, not downloaded full-text papers
project_scope: Motion definition -> contact and inverse dynamics -> conditional muscle tensions -> within-muscle comparison. No physiological activation, EMG, fatigue or injury predictions.

items.title: RTMPose / RTMLib
items.input: Video frames and athlete bounding boxes; Halpe26 includes toe and heel keypoints.
items.output: 2D keypoints and confidence scores; no measured depth or forces.
items.reuse: Independent tracking check for the crouch/tuck phases where MediaPipe selected background legs. Installed only in the isolated reference-tracking environment.
items.limits: Manual athlete boxes do not eliminate occlusion or keypoint errors. Estimated keypoints require frame review, and cannot establish calibrated 3D dynamics.

items.title: OpenCap: Human movement dynamics from smartphone videos
items.input: Two or more synchronized, calibrated camera views; subject dimensions; a musculoskeletal model.
items.output: 3D kinematics, modeled contacts, joint mechanics and conditional muscle-force estimates.
items.reuse: Separate video kinematics from dynamic simulation; inspect the kinetics example and contact/trajectory-tracking workflow.
items.limits: Validation applies to the reported tasks and conditions. It does not validate our single-view box jump or 240 kg squat. Its physiological outputs are outside our present scope.

items.title: OpenSim Moco: Musculoskeletal optimal control
items.input: Rigid-body model, muscle paths, external contacts, task goals and optionally a reference trajectory.
items.output: Prescribed, tracked or predicted motions and muscle-driven solutions, depending on the formulation.
items.reuse: The squat-to-stand example is a concrete reference for movement definition, dynamic solution and comparing a model modification.
items.limits: The teaching example is simplified, not a validated full-body loaded high-/low-bar/front squat. We would borrow the mechanics formulation without adding physiological activation or fatigue predictions.

items.title: Pose2Sim: An open-source Python package for multiview markerless kinematics
items.input: Calibrated multi-view video and 2D body observations.
items.reuse: Camera calibration, triangulation, tracking QC and musculoskeletal IK before any force calculation.
items.limits: A kinematics workflow does not by itself identify contact forces or muscle tensions. Single-view depth ambiguity remains in our current source video.

items.title: AddBiomechanics: Automating model scaling, inverse kinematics, and inverse dynamics from human motion data through sequential optimization
items.input: Optical marker trajectories; corresponding measured ground-reaction forces for the dynamics fit.
items.output: Scaled geometry, marker registration, kinematics, adjusted inertial properties and inverse dynamics.
items.reuse: Quantify root residuals and fit motion/inertia to measured forces rather than treating force balance alone as human-motion validation.
items.limits: This is not a direct video-to-individual-muscle-force tool. Our video reference has no measured force plates, so its measured-force validation cannot be transferred.

items.title: MyoConverter
items.kind: Open-source model conversion and validation tools
items.output: MuJoCo model conversion and optimization of muscle path/force properties.
items.reuse: Compare muscle lengths, moment arms and force behavior across engines before trusting tension magnitudes.
items.limits: Conversion has documented limitations for contacts, moving/conditional path points and some actuators. Successful conversion does not validate every muscle path or exercise.

items.title: Direct Methods for Predicting Movement Biomechanics Based Upon Optimal Control Theory with Implementation in OpenSim
items.input: Eight-segment, 48-muscle model; maximum-height jumping task and optimal-control assumptions.
items.output: Predicted jumping kinematics and ground reactions compared with experimental trajectories.
items.reuse: A jumping-specific reference for dynamic consistency and time-history validation, not just matching peak values.
items.limits: It addresses maximum-height jumping, not our complete box approach, tuck and supported landing. Code availability was not established in this collection.

items.title: Sky Higher: Dynamic Optimization of Maximum Jump Height
items.input: Simplified lower-body muscle model, foot-ground spheres and optional shoulder-torque arms.
items.output: Optimized takeoff and ballistic COM height.
items.reuse: Keep post-takeoff COM motion ballistic while limb rearrangement changes foot clearance. Useful separation for box jumps.
items.limits: An educational simplified model, not a quantitative reference for our full-body individual muscle forces or a 160 cm box height.

items.title: A Biomechanical Comparison Between a High and Low Barbell Placement on Net Joint Moments, Kinematics, Muscle Forces, and Muscle-Specific Moments in 3 Repetition Maximum Back Squats
items.input: Twelve trained men; standardized stance; high- and low-bar 3RM trials; motion capture and force plates.
items.output: Inverse-dynamic joint moments and statically optimized individual muscle forces.
items.reuse: Closest empirical comparison to the proposed high-/low-bar muscle-tension study.
items.limits: No significant lower-limb force/moment differences were found under this protocol. Do not force our model to produce a large style effect. Model-estimated muscle forces are not directly measured tensions. Abstract reviewed; numerical full-text tables not yet extracted.

items.title: Effect of squat depth and barbell load on relative muscular effort in squatting
items.input: Ten strength-trained women; 50-90% 1RM; squat joint moments and angle-matched maximum voluntary torques.
items.output: Joint-level relative muscular effort as net moment divided by angle-matched maximum torque.
items.reuse: Separate depth and load in the comparison design and match the mechanical quantity being compared.
items.limits: RME is a joint torque ratio, not individual muscle activation or direct tendon tension. Its strength-normalized metric is outside our present output scope. Abstract reviewed.

items.title: A biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals
items.input: Fifteen trained participants; motion, force and surface EMG during front/back squats.
items.output: Net knee forces and moments, with EMG as a separate measurement.
items.reuse: External bar placement, knee compression/shear and posture checks for the future front-squat branch.
items.limits: Do not substitute its EMG for muscle tension or generalize a relative-load protocol to an equal-100 kg comparison without matching conditions. Abstract reviewed.
